message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic, modern, and cult‑favorite horror films you might enjoy:

| Year | Title | Why it’s worth watching |
|------|-------|------------------------|
| 1960 | **Psycho** (dir. Alfred Hitchcock) | A masterclass in suspense and psychological terror. |
| 1978 | **The Shining** (dir. Stanley Kubrick) | A chilling blend of supernatural dread and human breakdown. |
| 1984 | **The Thing** (dir. John Carpenter) | A tense, atmospheric paranoia thriller with groundbreaking practical effects. |
| 1999 | **The Sixth Sense** (dir. M. Night Shyamalan) | A twist‑heavy story that keeps you guessing until the end. |
| 2002 | **28 Days Later** (dir. Danny Boyle) | A fast‑paced, post‑apocalyptic horror that redefined the zombie genre. |
| 2004 | **Saw** (dir. James Wan) | A gritty, puzzle‑based horror that sparked a long‑running franchise. |
| 2007 | **Paranormal Activity** (dir. Oren Peli) | Low‑budget, found‑footage style that delivers genuine chills. |
| 2010 | **The Conjuring** (dir. James Wan) | A well‑crafted haunted‑house story with strong character arcs. |
| 2013 | **It Follows** (dir. David Robert Mitchell) | A fresh take on the “invisible threat” trope with a haunting soundtrack. |
| 2015 | **The Witch** (dir. Robert Eggers) | A slow‑burning, period‑accurate horror that feels like a living nightmare. |
| 2017 | **Get Out** (dir. Jordan Peele) | A smart, socially‑aware horror that blends satire with genuine terror. |
| 2018 | **A Quiet Place** (dir. John Krasinski) | A tense, sound‑driven thriller that keeps you on edge. |
| 2020 | **Midsommar** (dir. Ari Aster) | A daylight horror that turns a sunny festival into a nightmare. |
| 2021 | **The Invisible Man** (dir. Leigh Whannell) | A modern retelling of a classic tale with strong feminist undertones. |
| 2022 | **Nope** (dir. Jordan Peele) | A genre‑blending film that mixes horror, sci‑fi, and social commentary. |
| 2023 | **Evil Dead Rise** (dir. Lee Cronin) | A fresh, gritty take on the iconic franchise with intense gore. |

Feel free to pick based on your preferred sub‑genre—whether you like psychological thrillers, supernatural scares, or gore‑heavy slashers. Enjoy the chills!
